name: Stewed Oysters
description: Historical recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Add a pint of hot water to the liquor drained from 2 quarts of oysters
Put a little salt and pepper with it
Set over the fire and let it boil up once
Turn in the oysters and let them cook for not more than five minutes, or until the gills begin to crimp
Watch carefully for this stage, as every second beyond it means injury to the flavor of the oyster
Add 2 tablespoons of butter and a large cup of boiling milk
Take from the fire immediately and serve as soon as possible
Never let them stand at the back of the stove and keep warm

source.originalInstructions:
1. Add a pint of hot water to the liquor drained from 2 quarts of oysters
2. Put a little salt and pepper with it
3. Set over the fire and let it boil up once
4. Turn in the oysters and let them cook for not more than five minutes, or until the gills begin to crimp
5. Watch carefully for this stage, as every second beyond it means injury to the flavor of the oyster
6. Add 2 tablespoons of butter and a large cup of boiling milk
7. Take from the fire immediately and serve as soon as possible
8. Never let them stand at the back of the stove and keep warm
